headline: Researchers at South Korea's Gachon University found that AI models that predict drug toxicity may look more accurate than they are because near-identical molecules sit in both their training and test data.
score_reason: Solid benchmark study with a clear caution for the field, but narrow audience and no outside review reported.
importance_line: Drug developers and regulators who rely on toxicity predictions get a warning that reported accuracy may be inflated, though the finding comes from one team and one small dataset gave noisy results.
summary: Scienmag, as relayed by Bioengineer.org, reports that Gachon University researchers built a benchmark called ToxBench and found that accuracy on the Tox21 dataset fell by 0.057 to 0.079 points (on a standard score called AUROC) when structurally similar molecules were kept out of the test set. The authors say a substantial share of reported progress in toxicity prediction may reflect this leakage, while one smaller dataset, ClinTox, gave results too noisy to rank the methods.
notes: Article carries Scienmag's text (credited at the end); Scienmag is named as source. Score kept at 5.
